item.title: Liverpool told to pay €40m to sign defender in January
item.description: Liverpool told to pay €40m to sign defender in January Liverpool tracking Ismaelo Ganiou as AC Milan circle €40m Lens defender Liverpool’s recruitment team appear to be casting the net widely ahead of the January window, with France once again emerging as a fertile market for young talent. Credit to Gazzetta Dello Sport, which reports that RC Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou is attracting serious attention, with AC Milan also firmly in the picture and a fee of around €40m seemingly enough to strike a deal. From Liverpool’s side, the logic is easy to follow. The club has already leaned into the French market in recent windows and there is a growing sense that more business from that pipeline could follow. Ganiou, 21, is understood to be admired for his versatility, with the ability to operate at centre-back and right-back particularly appealing to clubs seeking depth without compromising tactical flexibility. French market remains central to Liverpool plans There is a broader pattern developing around Liverpool’s scouting in France. A number of names have already surfaced, particularly in midfield and defence, and the profile is familiar, young, high-upside footballers with room to develop and potential resale strength. Lamine Camara has been mentioned as one of the midfield options under consideration, while Arthur Avom and Mahamadou Nagida are also part of the wider picture. That does not automatically mean deals are close across the board. As ever, admiration and active negotiations are different stages entirely. Yet the volume of reporting around Ligue 1 talents does indicate where much of Liverpool’s attention currently lies. Why Ganiou fits Liverpool recruitment model Ganiou looks like the kind of player modern recruitment departments value highly. He is young, tactically aware and sufficiently composed in possession to contribute to build-up play. Those traits matter even more for a side that expects defenders to be comfortable defending space and progressing the ball under pressure. The reported €40m valuation will naturally shape the conversation. For a 21-year-old defender still building his reputation, it is a meaningful fee. Equally, in the current market, a player capable of covering multiple positions and growing within an elite environment can quickly look like sound value. Photo IMAGO AC Milan interest could test Liverpool resolve Milan’s presence in the race is worth noting. When a club of that stature is prepared to engage, the market can move quickly. Liverpool may admire the player, but timing, squad priorities and the final structure of any package would all influence whether interest becomes something more concrete. For now, this feels like a situation to monitor closely. Liverpool are clearly active in France, and Ganiou is another name placed prominently on that list. item.title: Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma
item.description: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala sits on the bench prior to the start of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich are not ruling out the sale of Jamal Musiala as fresh statements from supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have escalated the situation surrounding the midfielder. Musiala has been struggling with fitness since a serious injury at last year's Club World Cup, which forced him to miss half of the 2025-26 season. He made his comeback from yet another injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday evening. However, there are concerns over his health after he collapsed earlier this year during two pre-season games. He later went public about a neurological condition. "He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal," Rummenigge said after the draw with Cologne. He said that selling the player "it's not out of the question. We suspect it will be difficult for him to get back to his previous level." However, Rummenigge added that he can't imagine another club would buy Musiala "under these circumstances. We have to think about the financial implications." Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness recently has also expressed doubts whether Musiala would ever return to his previous level of play. "He has an illness that is not easily curable, but can be controlled to some extent with medication. But whether he will ever again have the performance level he once had..." "But now he is still getting paid. Just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: what he can now deliver is no longer what was in the contract," he said referring to Musiala's deal until 2030. Hoeness was criticized for his statements, but Rummenigge backed the remarks. "Uli's wording was correct. Very serious and fair. We have an interest in seeing him return and play well. If that doesn't happen, then we will have to think about the situation," he said.

item.title: Elliot Anderson scores but Man City frustrated by Fulham
item.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Elliot Anderson scores but Man City frustrated by Fulham») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Elliot Anderson struck as Manchester City ended their losing run but more points were dropped as Fulham claimed a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. After Erling Haaland had an equalizer controversially disallowed, England midfielder Anderson netted with a sweet volley just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s well-crafted opener. It was enough to end City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but left them without a win in the competition for five weeks after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row. The main talking point was Haaland’s disallowed goal after 25 minutes, when the Norwegian prodded home from close range after a fumble by Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. To City’s frustration, the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. The draw ended Fulham’s run of 20 consecutive defeats against City in all competitions and continued their recent upturn in form under Alvaro Arbeloa, with the Cottagers now unbeaten in five Premier League games.

item.title: 3 keys to a Jets win at the Chargers in Week 11
item.description: The New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers enter Week 11 with a lot on the line. That's probably strange to say for two teams with a combined 16 losses through the first 11 weeks of the NFL season. In total, they have met 39 times, with the first meeting coming in 1960. That includes two postseason clashes. New York won both playoff meetings, but the Chargers hold a 24-14-1 advantage in the all-time series, with the tie coming in 1964. It's been a long time since the Jets won, dropping five straight in the series. Their last victory came in 2011, while the most recent meeting ended in a loss in 2023. This seems like an opportunity for New York to finally take one, but head coach Aaron Glenn's squad has taught us that nothing with this team is guaranteed. Still, expect Jets fans to find their way in front of a television anyway. The Jets (2-8) need more than a few promising stretches to finally put a game away. If they want to leave Los Angeles (1-8) with a victory. Here are Jets Wire's five keys to pulling off a win against the Chargers: Jets must take advantage of a team playing on a short week The Chargers have the advantage of playing at home, but they also have considerably less time to recover and prepare after Monday night's road victory. A short week can take a toll, particularly on a defense that must repeatedly defend long drives and deal with the physical demands of stopping the run. This is where the Jets could find an advantage. Establishing the rushing attack, moving the chains, and forcing Los Angeles' defense to spend more time on the field would help New York control the tempo. The Chargers have struggled when allowing explosive plays, and the Jets need to take advantage of that vulnerability rather than abandoning the ground game when opportunities are there. Keeping the offense ahead of the chains would also make life easier for whoever starts at quarterback. The Jets don't need to turn this into a shootout. They need to make the Chargers work for every possession while taking advantage of a defense playing on short rest. Stabilizing quarterback play Geno Smith left Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills with an ankle injury after previously being evaluated for a concussion. That opened the door for Cade Klubnik, who completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, but he was sacked three times and threw an interception. Smith seems set to return against Los Angeles, but his availability remains uncertain. Regardless of who gets the start, the Jets need a more stable performance under center. That means protecting the football, avoiding unnecessary pressure and giving the offense opportunities to stay on the field. The red-zone issues also have to improve. item.title: 3 keys to a Bills win vs. the Dolphins in Week 11
item.description: The Buffalo Bills are looking to stay in the win column in Week 11 as they head back home to take on the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium. The Bills (8-1) have won their last five games and are trying to keep the momentum going. How can Buffalo get the upper hand against the Dolphins (1-8)? Here are Bills Wire's three keys to victory in Week 11: Efficient passing Last week against the New York Jets, Josh Allen completed just 52.4% of his passes (11-for-21), recorded a passer rating of 80.7, and threw an interception. While Allen scored twice with his legs and the Bills ran away with the game, it wasn't an efficient game from him. This week, he'll have a chance to bounce back against another divisional rival. This year, the Dolphins are allowing the highest completion percentage for opposing quarterbacks in the NFL (73.7%). Allen and the passing game have a chance to get right at an important part of the season. Work the ground game James Cook continues to be the workhorse for the Bills offense, having at least 18 carries in seven of the last eight games for Buffalo. Last week, he ran for 157 yards and a touchdown, including a 74-yard house call to put the Jets to bed. The Dolphins have struggled on defense this year. They have the 27th-ranked run defense according to DVOA. The Bills should look to take control of this one and pound the rock. Perhaps they'll look to involve Ray Davis more out of the backfield in this one with a short week coming up for the Chiefs Thanksgiving matchup. Keep beating up on backup QBs The Bills defense has caught a break recently. Over their last three games, the've faced a backup QB in every matchup due to injury. In Week 8, they faced both Tyley Huntley and Joe Fagnano of the Ravens after Lamar Jackson went down. In Week 9 against the Vikings, they faced Carson Wentz. And, in Week 10, Geno Smith exited and they faced rookie Cade Clubnik. The Bills defense has stepped up in a major way the past three weeks after a rocky start to the season. They didn't allow a single touchdown in all three games. But, how much of it is from facing low-level offenses and how much should be credited to the defense for turning things around? It is more of the same for the Bills this week as they'll get Dolphins rookie QB Kyle McCord out of Syracuse after Malik Willis was put on IR . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Mets have received trade interest in Mark Vientos , but a deal does not appear imminent. The Mets tendered the first baseman and designated hitter a contract for 2027 on Friday, keeping him under club control. New York tendered Vientos before Friday’s 5 p.m. ET deadline. The 26-year-old is eligible for salary arbitration for the first time this offseason. The Mets can still trade him while they weigh their options at first base and designated hitter. Vientos hit 27 home runs during his 2024 breakout and carried that power into the postseason. His production declined over the next two seasons, leaving his role in Queens less certain heading into 2027. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Athletic’s Will Sammon shared an update Friday on X, formerly Twitter, revealing where things stood with Vientos after the Mets tendered him a contract. “Within: Mets have received some trade interest in Vientos. However, no deal involving him appears imminent.” Vientos hit .212 with 13 home runs and a .652 OPS in 87 games in 2026. A fractured right hand limited his playing time, though he posted an .809 OPS vs. left-handed pitching. The Mets also have Jorge Polanco and Jared Young as options at first base and designated hitter. Injuries limited Polanco to 37 games in 2026. Polanco remains under contract for 2027, so the club already has a veteran alternative. Young gives New York a left-handed hitter who can fill either spot. Vientos is out of minor league options, which limits how the Mets can manage their roster. They would have to expose him to waivers before sending him to the minors. The tender keeps him in the organization while New York evaluates its lineup. After a brutal 2026 season, the Mets wants to right the ship in 2027. If Vientos stays in Queens, his success against left-handed pitching gives New York a clear way to use his bat. item.title: Berrada insists Manchester United signings made squad 'fundamentally better' despite relegation fight
item.description: Berrada insists Manchester United signings made squad 'fundamentally better' despite relegation fight Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted the club's recent signings have made the squad 'fundamentally better', even with United sitting 18th in the Premier League table . Berrada sat down Sky Sports to discuss the club's start to the season, the sacking of Michael Carrick and the criticism aimed at United's leadership. United dismissed Carrick during the November international break and appointed Mauricio Pochettino , whose first match in charge is away at Liverpool tomorrow. It is the third season in a row in which the club have changed head coach mid-campaign. Recruitment has been a particular flashpoint. Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised technical director Jason Wilcox for not preparing the team well enough in the transfer window, while Bruno Fernandes took aim at the methods of Carrick and his coaching staff. 'We will not spend just for the sake of it' Berrada nonetheless defended United's business. He named Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Santos, Karl Darlow and returning loanee Marcus Rashford as additions that had improved the group. "In our view Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Karl Darlow, as well as Marcus Rashford, have made the squad fundamentally better."When we find the right opportunity, we will spend money. But again, we won't spend for the sake of it." - Omar Berrada 'I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction' United finished third in the Premier League last season to secure Champions League football, but are in the relegation places after 10 games in 2026/27. Despite that, Berrada said he was confident the club were heading in the right direction. "100%. I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table. It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward. "But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction."

item.title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
item.description: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. item.title: Incredible number of Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets still on sale on Saturday afternoon
item.description: Jacob Murphy Newcastle United v Arsenal I thought I would have a look just in case, see if by chance any Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were available on Saturday afternoon. Just in case you aren’t aware, the club allow Newcastle United season ticket holders to sell their tickets for individual Premier League games. This was a very positive move by the club as it means that seats don’t need to be left empty if a season ticket holder is ill for example. Using the online club system, season ticket holders can make their ticket available for a league match, with Newcastle United members then able to go onto the NUFC official ticketing site (you have to be then logged in as a member to see the tickets that are available) to buy. The club also make money from this. As I understand it, the fan (season ticket holder) selling the ticket is credited with the pro rata match price of their season ticket and if the ticket is then bought by a member, they are charged the far higher single ticket price, with the club banking the difference. As a member, I had no luck in the ballot for Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets. The same when it came to the queue sale. The demand was huge, I had a ridiculously high number for the queue sale and stood no chance, along with countless thousands of other Newcastle United members. Anyway, I have just went onto the club’s ticketing site (just before 2pm on Saturday) and I couldn’t believe how many Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were on sale! To be honest, I wasn’t expecting there to be any, I was just looking in the vain hope I might hit very lucky. What I found was I had a choice of all around St James’ Park ! All four stands with plenty tickets up for sale from season ticket holders. I snapped up a couple for me and my mate for the East Stand and after sending this article into The Mag I will be heading off to the Toon to meet up with the lads (mostly season ticket holders) for some pre-match refreshments. After buying our tickets I counted up all the Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets that season ticket holders are trying to sell and there were 147 available (it had been 149 I guess before I snapped up ours). Apologies for my wonky photography skills but the red areas are where there were Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets available just over three and a half hours before the match… Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets I am over the moon getting these tickets but at the same time absolutely stunned that so many season ticket holders are trying to flog their tickets. Is it because they think Arsenal will win? Is it because it is a bit chilly? Is it because they will get too upset seeing Bruno Guimaraes in an Arsenal shirt? Anyway, if you are a member who didn’t get a ticket for today’s match, log onto the official ticketing site and take your pick!!

item.description: Match Report And Player Ratings: Manchester City 1-1 Fulham (Premier League) It was another dreary first-half from Enzo Maresca’s side, with Fulham causing all manner of problems and taking the lead through Rodrigo Muniz. The Blues were reinvigorated in the second-half and equalised through Elliot Anderson, but didn’t do enough to push on for a winner and thus were left with another poor result. Fulham’s high press was severely disrupting Manchester City ’s attempts to play out from the back in the early exchanges, but some inroads were made and the Blues generated the game’s first half-chances, Erling Haaland’s shot blocked by David Affengruber and Nico O’Reilly seeing an effort deflect into the side netting. But for the fourth Premier League game in a row, City fell behind inside the opening 20 minutes. Ex-Blue Oscar Bobb escaped the attentions of Elliot Anderson and fed Muniz, who deceived Abdukodir Khusanov and stuck the ball into Gianluigi Donnarumma’s top corner to deepen Maresca’s concerns. City thought they had had their equaliser soon after when Iliman Ndiaye’s cross found Haaland and his initial shot was fumbled by Bernd Leno, allowing the Norwegian to follow up, but the referee deemed that the goalkeeper had two hands on it at the time of the striker’s second kick, meaning a foul and no goal. Fulham almost took advantage of that reprieve to double their lead, Bobb again leading a breakaway and only Ruben Dias’ late intervention clearing Josh King’s dangerous low cross. It was a pitiful first half-hour and Manchester City fans inside the Etihad Stadium began booing and jeering at the players’ unwillingness to press high and take the ball off of a Fulham side meandering around in their own half. City won the ball, Phil Foden found Haaland in behind and he blazed over a massive chance. City’s pace had finally improved, and Elliot Anderson succeeded in breaking through the lines to find Nico O’Reilly in a crossing position, but Haaland was again wayward, this time via a deflection. Ruben Dias put a free header over from the resulting corner. Despite that pressure, City were lucky not to go 2-0 down on the brink of the break. O’Reilly switched off in the box and it broke for Bobb, who was denied a goal on his return to the Etihad by a big Donnarumma save. item.description: New York Giants defensive back Jevon Holland and Deonte Banks celebrate after an interception. | Getty Images There were, if not outright concerns, certainly questions about how good the New York Giants defense could be in 2026. Between edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, as well as off-ball linebackers Tremaine Edmunds, Arvell Reese, and Micah McFadden, the Giants’ linebacking corps was expected to be one of the best in the NFL. And the hope was that their defensive line would at least be serviceable after the addition of veteran defensive tackles D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. The bigger questions were about the Giants’ secondary, particularly after Cor’Dale Flott left in free agency. 2025 free agents Paulson Adebo and Jevon Holland hadn’t panned out in their first years as Giants, while 2023 first round pick Deonte Banks had regressed badly under DC Shane Bowen and was considered a bust. The Giants signed former Cleveland Browns and Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome II, as well as former Baltimore Ravens safety Ar’Darius Washington, in the 2026 free agency period and drafted Tennessee cornerback Colton Hood in the second round of the draft. However, those moves weren’t viewed as much more than Band-Aids for a Giants’ secondary, and national commentors suggested that the Giants’ scondary could be putrid in the first year of John Harbaugh’s rebuild. Fast-forward nine games, and the Giants’ secondary has been much, much , better than anticipated under Dennard Wilson, Donald D’Alesio, and Addison Lynch. The Giants are currently fielding the NFL’s fourth-best defense in total yardage allowed (2,751 total yards). They’re third-best in passing yardage allowed per game (184.1 yards per game), second in yards per completion allowed (9.8 yards per completion), and 2nd in yards per attempt allowed (6.2 yards per attempt). The Giants are accomplishing this feat with smothering coverage from their starting corners. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change

And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion.
